heading.en: Why does hot tea cool fast at first?
heading.kn: ಬಿಸಿ ಚಹಾ ಮೊದಲು ಏಕೆ ಬೇಗ ತಣ್ಣಗಾಗುತ್ತದೆ?

hook.en: A cup of tea drops from very hot to warm quickly, but then takes a long time to reach room temperature. The rate of *cooling* depends on how much hotter it is than the room.
hook.kn: ಚಹಾ ಬಹಳ ಬಿಸಿಯಿಂದ ಉಗುರುಬೆಚ್ಚಗೆ ಬೇಗ ಇಳಿಯುತ್ತದೆ, ಆದರೆ ಕೋಣೆಯ ತಾಪ ತಲುಪಲು ಬಹಳ ಸಮಯ ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತದೆ. ತಂಪಾಗುವ ದರ ಕೋಣೆಗಿಂತ ಎಷ್ಟು ಬಿಸಿ ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸಿದೆ.

say.en: A cup of tea drops from very hot to warm quickly, but then takes a long time to reach room temperature. The rate of cooling depends on how much hotter it is than the room. In this lesson: State Newton's law of cooling.
Use the average form to solve cooling problems.

body.en: The rate of loss of heat of a body is proportional to the difference between its temperature T and the temperature T_s of its surroundings, provided the difference is small: −dQ/dt = k(T − T_s). The temperature therefore falls exponentially towards T_s, fast at first and slowly later.
body.kn: ವಸ್ತುವಿನ ಉಷ್ಣ ನಷ್ಟದ ದರ ಅದರ ತಾಪ ಮತ್ತು ಸುತ್ತಲಿನ ತಾಪದ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸಕ್ಕೆ ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿರುತ್ತದೆ (ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸ ಚಿಕ್ಕದಿದ್ದಾಗ). ತಾಪ ಘಾತೀಯವಾಗಿ ಇಳಿಯುತ್ತದೆ.

The temperature therefore falls exponentially towards T s, fast at first and slowly later. Valid for small temperature differences.

say.en: Cooling curve: exponential fall to T s.
A cup of tea at 90 degrees cools in a room at 30. It cools fast at first, then more and more slowly.
The rate of cooling is proportional to the excess temperature over the surroundings, when the excess is small.
Solving, the excess temperature decays exponentially.
For problems use the average form. A body cools from 80 to 50 degrees in 5 minutes in a room at 20. First find K.
Now the time to cool from 60 to 30 degrees: the excess is smaller, so it takes longer: 9 minutes.
A check: log of the excess temperature against time is a straight line with slope minus K.

narration.en: A hot body loses heat at a rate proportional to how much hotter it is than its surroundings: dT/dt = −k(T − T_s). So it cools fast at first and slowly near room temperature; the difference halves every ln2/k. A lid lowers k.
narration.kn: ಬಿಸಿ ಕಾಯ ಸುತ್ತಮುತ್ತಲಿಗಿಂತ ಎಷ್ಟು ಬಿಸಿಯಾಗಿದೆಯೋ ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಅನುಪಾತದ ದರದಲ್ಲಿ ಉಷ್ಣ ಕಳೆಯುತ್ತದೆ: dT/dt = −k(T − T_s). ಹಾಗಾಗಿ ಮೊದಲು ವೇಗವಾಗಿ, ಕೊಠಡಿ ತಾಪದ ಹತ್ತಿರ ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ತಣ್ಣಗಾಗುತ್ತದೆ; ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸ ಪ್ರತಿ ln2/k ಗೆ ಅರ್ಧವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಮುಚ್ಚಳ k ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: A body cools from 80 °C to 60 °C in 5 min in a room at 20 °C. How long will it take to cool from 60 °C to 40 °C?

say.en: Let us solve this together. A body cools from 80 degrees Celsius to 60 degrees Celsius in 5 minutes in a room at 20 degrees Celsius. How long will it take to cool from 60 degrees Celsius to 40 degrees Celsius?
First interval: 20 over 5 equals K70 minus 20 gives K equals 0.08 minutes to the power minus 1.
Second interval: 20 over t equals 0.08 times 50 minus 20 equals 2.4.
t equals 20 over 2.4 is approximately 8.3 minutes.
So the answer is About 8.3 minutes.
